The lower edge passes through (0,0) and (22,-3), with a slope of -3/22, so the equation is y = -(3/22)x. Let the two lines intersect: 3 + (7/22)x = -(3/22)x, obtaining 3 = -(10/22)x, therefore x = -6.6. Substitute back into the lower-edge equation, y = -(3/22)(-6.6) = 0.9. The ratio of the camera height to the real height is equal to the ratio of the horizon line on this vertical edge: h/H = (0.9 - 0)/(3 - 0). So h = 3 × 0.9/3 = 0.9 m.

raw_record.question_text: These days, there are so many stylish rectangular home-designs (see figure A). It is possible from the outline of those houses in their picture to estimate with good precision where the camera was. Consider an outline in one photograph of a rectangular house which has height H = 3 meters (see figure B for square-grid coordinates). Assume that the camera size is negligible, how high above the ground (in meters) was the camera at the moment this picture was taken?

method.method_draft: Use the long left side of the house outline to find the horizon/eye level. From figure B, read the two corresponding receding edges of the rectangular side face: the top edge joins (0,3) to (22,10), and the bottom edge joins (0,0) to (22,-3). Extend these two image lines until they meet; their intersection is the vanishing point for that horizontal direction. Solving the two line equations gives an intersection with y-coordinate 0.9, so the camera eye level in the picture is y = 0.9. Then use the left vertical edge, whose bottom and top are labeled (0,0) and (0,3). Since the real vertical height of the house is H = 3 m, the camera height is the same fraction of the real height as the horizon level is between the projected bottom and top on a vertical edge: h/H = (0.9 - 0)/(3 - 0). Thus h = 3 * 0.9/3 = 0.9 m.

Let the two lines intersect: 3 + (7/22)x = -(3/22)x, obtaining 3 = -(10/22)x, therefore x = -6.6. Substitute back into the lower-edge equation, y = -(3/22)(-6.6) = 0.9. Therefore the horizon line in the figure is y = 0.9.

The left vertical edge goes from y=0 to y=3, corresponding to the real height of the house H=3 m. The ratio of the camera height to the real height is equal to the ratio of the horizon line on this vertical edge: h/H = (0.9 - 0)/(3 - 0). So h = 3 × 0.9/3 = 0.9 m.
